title: Nature Ice Palace Hintertux Glacier
name: Nature Ice Palace Hintertux Glacier
kurzbeschreibung: The Natur Eis Palast at Hintertuxer Gletscher at 3,250 m: a globally unique ice cave deep inside glacier ice with a frozen lake and boat tour.
beschreibung:
Overview

The spectacular Natur Eis Palast is situated at a high-alpine elevation of approximately 3,250 metres directly beneath the Gefrorene Wand on the year-round snow-covered Hintertuxer Gletscher in the upper Zillertal (municipality of Tux, Bezirk Schwaz). Discovered by chance in 2007 by speleologist Roman Erler, this natural wonder is considered a globally unique, accessible crevasse and ice cave of entirely natural origin, never artificially carved from the ice. Deep inside the eternal ice, visitors enter a mystical, shimmering blue wonderland of frozen water.

Glacier Cathedral & Ice Boat Tour

The secured walking tour leads visitors over ladders and footbridges up to 35 metres beneath the ski slopes of the glacier. Inside, a constant temperature of exactly zero degrees Celsius prevails year-round. Visitors can marvel at metre-long, crystal-clear icicles, massive glistening ice crystals, and frozen waterfalls. The up to 15-metre-high Gletscherkathedrale (Glacier Cathedral) captivates with its intense, natural turquoise blue, created by the refraction of light through centuries-old, oxygen-poor firn ice. The ultimate highlight is the underground glacier lake: on this crystal-clear meltwater lake, guided guests glide silently through the ice grotto aboard an inflatable raft; adventurous visitors can even book stand-up paddleboarding or ice swimming in the frigid waters.

Visit & Getting There

The Natur Eis Palast is open 365 days a year; guided tours take place daily without advance reservation between 09:30 and 15:30 (standard tour duration approx. 60 minutes; minimum age for children 6 years). Natur Eis Palast guided tour admission (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €39.00, children (6 to 14 years) approx. €18.00. Ascent is via the three sections of the cable car (Gletscherbus 1, 2, and 3 up to Gefrorene Wand top station, approx. €45.00 for pedestrian round trip). By car: via the B169 into the Zillertal to Mayrhofen, then via Tuxer Landesstraße to Hintertux (large car park at the valley station). By public transport: Zillertalbahn railway to Mayrhofen, continuing with the Tuxer Sportbus directly to the glacier cable car.

Tips

Since temperatures inside remain constant at 0 °C, warm winter clothing, a hat, gloves, and sturdy hiking boots with good tread are mandatory (helmets and safety gear are provided on site). Combine this ice adventure with a visit to the Panoramaterrasse 3.250 m at the top station of Gletscherbus 3 for unobstructed panoramic views stretching as far as the Dolomites.
